2053.subject: Zoology
2053.text: Which of the following waste products in grasshopper is not excreted and is used in other metabolic activities?
2053.sol: Excretory organs of grasshopper are the Malpighian tubules and the main excretory product is uric acid. Malpighian tubules of insects such as grasshoppers not only help to excrete the waste but also function to conserve water, which is then used in other metabolic activities. In the Malpighian tubules, bicarbonates of potassium and sodium, water and uric acid are formed during the process of excretion. A large amount of water and bicarbonates of potassium and sodium are reabsorbed by the cells of Malpighian tubules and then transferred to the blood (haemolymph). Uric acid is carried to the alimentary canal of the insect and is finally passed out through anus.

2214.subject: Zoology
2214.text: Assertion : Some marine animals find it difficult to live in fresh water and vice versa.Reason : Some animals can tolerate a narrow salinity range, while others can tolerate a wide salinity range.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
2214.sol: For aquatic organism salt concentration (measured as salinity in parts per thousand) is a major factor for their survival. Salinity of different aquatic habitats varies greatly. It is less than 5 per thousand parts, in inland waters, 30-35 per thousand parts in the sea and more than 100 per thousand parts in some hypersaline lagoons. Many fresh water animals cannot live for long in sea water and vice versa because of the osmotic problems they would face due to the change in relative tonicity of the surrounding water with cytoplasm. It may result into endosmosis or exosmosis according to the conditions. The tolerance of organisms to the salinity range varies. Some organisms are tolerant of a wide range of salinities and are called euryhaline e.g. salmon, while some can tolerate only a narrow range of salinity i.e., stenohaline e.g., shark.

3438.subject: Chemistry
3438.text: Which of the following correctly represents copper sulphate pentahydrate?
3438.sol:
Chemical formula of copper sulphate pentahydrate \(\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4\right] \mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\).
Copper sulphate pentahydrate contains \(5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) that is 5 water of crystallisation. The 5 molecules of water present in the crystal framework of the molecule where four water molecules are coordinated to \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\) while one is hydrogen bonded with \(\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}\).
The copper (II) is bound to four water molecules in a square planar geometry and two oxygen atoms from two sulphate ions (one \(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\) is \(\mathrm{H}\) bonded here).
Hence, correct formula is \(\left[\mathrm{Cu}\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_4\right] \mathrm{SO}_4 \cdot \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\).

3453.subject: Chemistry
3453.text: Identify, from the following, the diamagnetic, tetrahedral complex
3453.sol:
(a) $\mathrm{Ni}$ in $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. $\because \quad \mathrm{C} \ell$ is a weak field ligand (high spin). It will not cause pairing of electrons. Hence, configuration of $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{C} \ell)_4\right]^{2-}$ is
Tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (i.e., paramagnetic) and has $s p^3$ hybridisation. (b) In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right],\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3$ is a bidentate ligand thus, give octahedral structure. (c) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, $\mathrm{Ni}$ exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. $\because \quad \mathrm{CN}^{-}$is a strong field ligand (low spin), causes pairing of electrons of $3 d$ orbital.
Hence, the structure of $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$ is square planar and it is diamagnetic. (d) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\right]$, $\mathrm{Ni}$ has zero oxidation state. i.e.,
$\mathrm{CO}$ is a strong field ligand causes rearrangement and pairing of electrons of $3 d$ and $4 s$ orbital.
Structure of $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4$ is tetrahedral with $s p^3$ hybridisation and it is diamagnetic. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

6949.text: The poles of the tangents to the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$ with respect to the circle $( x + 2{)}^{2} + y^{2} = 8$& lie on
6949.sol:
Given: ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 4$

${\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 8$

Equation of tangent at any point on the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 4$is

$xcos\theta + ysin\theta = r$

$xcos\theta + ysin\theta = 2 . . . \left(1\right)$

The polar of $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$w.r.t. ${\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 8$

$x{x}_{1} + y{y}_{1} + 2\left(x + {x}_{1}\right) - 4 = 0$

$⇒ \left({x}_{1} + 2\right)x + {y}_{1}y + 2\left({x}_{1} - 2\right) = 0 . . . \left(2\right)$

from equation $\left(1\right)$& $\left(2\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{cos\theta}{{x}_{1} + 2} = \dfrac{sin\theta}{{y}_{1}} = \dfrac{- 2}{2\left({x}_{1} - 2\right)}$

$cos\theta = - \dfrac{\left({x}_{1} + 2\right)}{\left({x}_{1} - 2\right)}$& $sin\theta = - \dfrac{y}{{x}_{1} - 2}$

${cos}^{2}\theta + {sin}^{2}\theta = \dfrac{{\left({x}_{1} + 2\right)}^{2}}{{\left({x}_{1} - 2\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{{{y}_{1}}^{2}}{{\left({x}_{1} - 2\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{\left({x}_{1} + 2\right)}^{2} + {{y}_{1}}^{2}}{{\left({x}_{1} - 2\right)}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ {{x}_{1}}^{2} + 4{x}_{1} + 4 + {{y}_{1}}^{2} = {{x}_{1}}^{2} - 4{x}_{1} + 4$

$⇒ {{y}_{1}}^{2} + 8{x}_{1} = 0$

$⇒ {y}^{2} + 8x = 0$

18670.text: The angle between the lines whose direction cosines are given by the equations $3 l+m+5 n=0,6 \mathrm{ nm}-2 \mathrm{n} l+5 l \mathrm{m}=0$ is
18670.sol:
The given equations are
$3 l+m+5 n=0$...(i)
and $6 \mathrm{mn}-2 \mathrm{n} l+5 l \mathrm{m}=0$...(ii)
From (i), we have $m=-3 l-5 n$.
Putting $\mathrm{m}=-3 l-5 \mathrm{n}$ in (ii),
we get $6(-3 l-5 n) n-2 n l+5 l(-3 l-5 n)=0\Rightarrow(n+l)(2 n+l)=0\Rightarrow$ either $l=-\mathrm{n}$ or $l=-2 \mathrm{n}$.
If $l=-n$, then putting $l=-n$ in (i), we obtain $m=-2 n$.
If $l=-2 \mathrm{n}$, then putting $l=-2 \mathrm{n}$ in (i), we obtain $\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{n}$.
Thus, the direction ratios of two lines are $-\mathrm{n},-2 \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n} and -2 \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n}$ i.e., $1,2,-1 and -2,1,1$.
Hence, the direction cosines are
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}, \frac{-1}{\sqrt{6}}$ or $\frac{-2}{\sqrt{6}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$. The angle $\theta$
between the lines is given by
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \times \frac{-2}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{-1}{\sqrt{6}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}=\frac{-1}{6} \\
& \Rightarrow \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{6}\right)
\end{aligned}$

19684.subject: Chemistry
19684.text: Structures of 3 Monosaccharides are given below. Two of them are Anomers. Identify the two Anomers.
options: II is the anomer of both I and II
19684.sol:
Anomers are a specific type of epimers that differ in configuration only at the anomeric carbon (the hemiacetal or hemiketal carbon).

In the given Fischer projections of cyclic monosaccharides, the anomeric carbon is the one attached to the ring oxygen and the hydroxyl group. By examining the structures, we observe that structure [I] and structure [III] have the same configuration at all chiral centers except for the anomeric carbon.

Specifically, in structure [I], the hydroxyl group at the anomeric position is on the right side, while in structure [III], the hydroxyl group at the anomeric position is on the left side. All other chiral centers (carbons 2, 3, and 4) maintain the same relative configuration in both [I] and [III].

Structure [II] differs from [I] and [III] at multiple chiral centers, meaning it is not an anomer of either. Therefore, [I] and [III] are the anomers.

Answer: I and III are Anomers

20669.subject: Chemistry
20669.text: What is the mole fraction of solute in a $5 \mathrm{ m}$ aqueous solution?
20669.sol:
A $5 \text{ m}$ aqueous solution means $5$ moles of solute are dissolved in $1 \text{ kg}$ ($1000 \text{ g}$) of solvent (water).

The number of moles of water ($n_{solvent}$) is calculated as:
$n_{solvent} = \dfrac{1000 \text{ g}}{18 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 55.56 \text{ mol}$

The mole fraction of the solute ($x_{solute}$) is given by the ratio of moles of solute to the total number of moles in the solution:
$x_{solute} = \dfrac{n_{solute}}{n_{solute} + n_{solvent}}$

$x_{solute} = \dfrac{5}{5 + 55.56} = \dfrac{5}{60.56}$

$x_{solute} \approx 0.08256$

21218.subject: Mathematics
21218.text: If $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{l}m x+1, x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2} \\ \sin x+n, x > \dfrac{\pi}{2}\end{array} \quad\right.$ is continuous at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, then
21218.sol:
For the function $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, the left-hand limit, right-hand limit, and the value of the function at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ must be equal.

The left-hand limit is given by $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}^{-}} (mx + 1) = m\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 1$.

The value of the function at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ is $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = m\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 1$.

The right-hand limit is given by $\lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}^{+}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2}^{+}} (\sin x + n) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + n = 1 + n$.

Equating the left-hand limit and the right-hand limit:

$\dfrac{m\pi}{2} + 1 = 1 + n$

Subtracting 1 from both sides:

$\dfrac{m\pi}{2} = n$

Solving for $m$:

$m = \dfrac{2n}{\pi}$.

Answer: $m=\dfrac{2 n}{\pi}$

21250.text: If $a$ is a real number such that $\int_\limits0^a x d x \leq a+4$ then
21250.sol:
The given integral is $\int_{0}^{a} x dx$.

Evaluating the definite integral:

$\left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{a} = \dfrac{a^2}{2} - 0 = \dfrac{a^2}{2}$

The given inequality is $\dfrac{a^2}{2} \leq a + 4$.

Multiplying by 2:

$a^2 \leq 2a + 8$

$a^2 - 2a - 8 \leq 0$

Factoring the quadratic expression:

$(a - 4)(a + 2) \leq 0$

The roots of the quadratic equation $a^2 - 2a - 8 = 0$ are $a = 4 and a = -2$.

For the inequality to hold, $a$ must lie between the roots, inclusive:

$-2 \leq a \leq 4$.

Answer: $-2 \leq a \leq 4$

Using the standard integral formula:

$\int e^{ax}\cos(bx + c)dx = \dfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2 + b^2}[a\cos(bx + c) + b\sin(bx + c)] + C$

Comparing the given integral $\int e^{2x}\cos(5x + 3)dx$ with the standard form, we get $a = 2$, $b = 5$, and $c = 3$.

22947.subject: Physics
22947.text: Internal energy of $\mathrm{n}_1$ moles of hydrogen at temperature T is equal to internal energy of $\mathrm{m}_2$ moles of helium at temperature 2T. The ratio $\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}$ is
22947.sol:
The internal energy $U$ of an ideal gas is given by $U = n C_V T$, where $n$ is the number of moles, $C_V$ is the molar heat capacity at constant volume, and $T$ is the temperature.

For hydrogen ($H_2$), which is a diatomic gas, the degrees of freedom $f = 5$. Thus, $C_{V, H_2} = \dfrac{f}{2} R = \dfrac{5}{2} R$. The internal energy is $U_1 = n_1 \times \dfrac{5}{2} R \times T$.

For helium ($He$), which is a monatomic gas, the degrees of freedom $f = 3$. Thus, $C_{V, He} = \dfrac{f}{2} R = \dfrac{3}{2} R$. The internal energy is $U_2 = n_2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} R \times (2T)$.

Equating the internal energies $U_1 = U_2$:

$n_1 \times \dfrac{5}{2} R \times T = n_2 \times \dfrac{3}{2} R \times 2T$

Simplifying the equation by cancelling $R$ and $T$ from both sides:

$n_1 \times \dfrac{5}{2} = n_2 \times 3$

Rearranging to find the ratio $\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}$:

$\dfrac{n_1}{n_2} = \dfrac{3}{5/2} = \dfrac{3 \times 2}{5} = \dfrac{6}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{6}{5}$

23015.text: A straight wire of mass 250 g and length 2.5 m carries a current of 4 A. It can be suspended in mid air by a uniform horizontal magnetic field of magnitude:
23015.sol:
The wire is suspended in mid-air, which implies that the magnetic force acting on the wire must balance the gravitational force acting on it.

The gravitational force $F_g$ acting on the wire is given by $F_g = mg$, where $m = 250 \text{ g} = 0.25 \text{ kg}$ and $g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$.

$F_g = 0.25 \times 9.8 = 2.45 \text{ N}$.

The magnetic force $F_m$ on a current-carrying wire in a uniform magnetic field is given by $F_m = IlB \sin(\theta)$. Since the magnetic field is horizontal and the wire is suspended, the force is perpendicular to the wire, so $\theta = 90^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $\sin(90^{{}^{\circ}}) = 1$.

$F_m = IlB$.

Equating the forces, $IlB = mg$.

$B = \dfrac{mg}{Il} = \dfrac{0.25 \times 9.8}{4 \times 2.5} = \dfrac{2.45}{10} = 0.245 \text{ T}$.

Answer: 0.245 T

23318.text: Two simple harmonic motions are represented by equations $y_1=0.5 \sin  \left[200 $\pi$ t+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$ and $y_1=0.5 \cos $\pi$ t$. The phase difference of the velocity of particle 1 with respect to the velocity of particle 2 is:
23318.sol:
The first equation is $y_1 = 0.5 \sin \left($200 $\pi$t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right). The velocity $v_1$ is given by the derivative \dfrac{dy_1}{dt} =$0.5 $\times$200 $\pi \cos \left($200 $\pi$t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) =$100 $\pi \sin \left($200 $\pi$t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).

The second equation is $y_2 = 0.5 \cos(\pit) = 0.5 \sin $\left(\pit + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).$The velocity $v_2$ is given by the derivative $\dfrac{dy_2}{dt} =0.5 \times \pi \cos \left(\pit + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) =0.5 \pi \sin \left(\pit + \dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) =0.5 \pi \sin(\pit + \pi).$

The phase of velocity $v_1$ is $\phi_1 = 200 \pit + \dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} =200 \pit + \dfrac{5\pi}{6}.$

The phase of velocity $v_2$ is $\phi_2 = \pit + \pi.$

The phase difference $\Delta \phi = \phi_$1 - \phi_2 = ($200 \pit + \dfrac{5\pi}{6}) - (\pit + \pi) =199 \pit - \dfrac{\pi}{6}.$

At $t=0$, the phase difference is $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}.$

Answer: $\dfrac{-\pi}{6}$

23355.subject: Physics
23355.text: Two light rays A and B travel from a medium into air at angles of incidence 15 degrees and 42 degrees respectively. In the medium, light travels 3 cm in 0.2 ns. Will there be total internal reflection? If so, which ray?
23355.sol:
The speed of light in the medium is $v = \dfrac{d}{t} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}}{0.2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}} = 1.5 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$.

The refractive index of the medium is $n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^{8}}{1.5 \times 10^{8}} = 2$.

The critical angle $\theta_{c}$ is given by $\sin(\theta_{c}) = \dfrac{n_{air}}{n_{medium}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Thus, $\theta_{c} = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$.

Total internal reflection occurs when the angle of incidence $i > \theta_{c}$.

For ray A, $i_{A} = 15^{{}^{\circ}} < 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, so no total internal reflection occurs.

For ray B, $i_{B} = 42^{{}^{\circ}} > 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, so total internal reflection occurs for ray B.

Answer: Yes, B

The logic gate described has the following truth table behavior:

When both inputs are high (1,1), the output is low (0).

When both inputs are low (0,0), the output is high (1).

This behavior corresponds to the NAND gate, which is the complement of the AND gate. The truth table for a NAND gate is as follows:

Since the output is low only when both inputs are high, and high otherwise, it matches the definition of a NAND gate.

23784.subject: Physics
23784.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a horizontal circle of radius $r$ under a centripetal force given by $\left(\dfrac{-K}{r^2}\right)$, where $K$ is a constant. Then
options: the total energy of the particle is $\left(\dfrac{-K}{2 r}\right)$
the kinetic energy of the particle is $\left(\dfrac{K}{r}\right)$
the potential energy of the particle is $\left(\dfrac{K}{2 r}\right)$
the kinetic energy of the particle is $\left(\dfrac{-K}{r}\right)$
23784.sol:
The centripetal force acting on the particle is given by $F = \dfrac{-K}{r^2}$. The magnitude of the centripetal force is $F_c = \dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{K}{r^2}$.

From this, the kinetic energy $K.E.$ is calculated as $K.E. = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{K}{r} \right) = \dfrac{K}{2r}$.

The potential energy $U$ is defined by $F = -\dfrac{dU}{dr}$. Integrating the force $F = -\dfrac{K}{r^2}$ with respect to $r$, we get $U = \int \dfrac{K}{r^2} dr = -\dfrac{K}{r}$.

The total energy $E$ is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy: $E = K.E. + U = \dfrac{K}{2r} - \dfrac{K}{r} = -\dfrac{K}{2r}$.

Comparing this with the given options, the total energy of the particle is $-\dfrac{K}{2r}$.

Answer: the total energy of the particle is $\left(\dfrac{-K}{2 r}\right)$

25284.text: The area of the region between the curves $y=\sqrt{\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}}$ and $y=\sqrt{\frac{1-\sin x}{\cos x}}$ bounded by the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ is

&

Put $\tan \frac{x}{2}=t$
$$

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2} \sec ^2 \frac{x}{2} d x & =d t \\

25621.text: Let $R = \left\{\left(\begin{cases}a & 3 & b \\ c & 2 & d \\ 0 & 5 & 0\end{cases}\right): a, b, c, d \in \left\{0, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19\right\}\right\}$. Then the number of invertible matrices in $R$ is
25621.sol:
Given,

$R = \left[\begin{cases}a & 3 & b \\ c & 2 & d \\ 0 & 5 & 0\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ | R | = - 5\left|\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right|$

We know that, for invertible matrices $\left|R\right| \ne 0$

Now $| R |$ can be zero in following cases:

(i) Two of $a, b, c, d$ are zeroes which can be ($a$ and $b$),($b$ and $d$),($d$ and $c$) or ($c$ and $a$)

$\to 4 \times {7}^{2}\text{ways} = 196$

(ii) Any three of $a, b, c, d$ are zeroes

$\to C3 4 \times 7 = 28$

(iii) All four of $a, b, c, d$ are zeroes

$\to 1$

(iv) All four of $a, b, c, d$ are non-zero but same number

$\to 7$

(v) When two are alike and $2$ other are alike (non-zero)

$\to 7{C}_{2} \times 2 \times 2 = 84$

Number of invertible matrices

$= {8}^{4} - 196 - 28 - 1 - 7 - 84 = 3780$

28045.text:
The equilibrium composition for the reaction

${PCl}_{3} + {Cl}_{2}\mathop{⇌}_{}{PCl}_{5}$ at $298K$ is given below:

${\left[{PCl}_{3}\right]}_{eq} = 0 . 2mol{L}^{- 1}, {\left[{Cl}_{2}\right]}_{eq} = 0 . 1mol{L}^{- 1}, {\left[{PCl}_{5}\right]}_{eq} = 0 . 40mol{L}^{- 1}$

If $0 . 2mol$ of ${Cl}_{2}$ is added at the same temperature, the equilibrium concentrations of ${PCl}_{5}$ is _____ $\times {10}^{– 2}mol{L}^{– 1}$

Given: ${K}_{c}$ for the reaction at $298K$ is $20$
28045.sol:
$\mathop{{PCl}_{3}\left(g\right)}_{0 . 2} + \mathop{{Cl}_{2}\left(g\right)}_{0 . 1}\mathop{⇌}_{}\mathop{{PCl}_{5}\left(g\right)}_{0 . 4}$

${K}_{c} = \dfrac{0 . 4}{0 . 2 \times 0 . 1} = 20$

If $0 . 2$ moles of ${Cl}_{2}$ is added. When reactant is added the reaction takes place in forward direction.

$20 = {K}_{c} = \dfrac{0 . 4 + X}{\left(0 . 3 - X\right)\left(0 . 2 - X\right)}$

$⇒ \left(0 . 4 + X\right) = 20\left(0 . 3 - X\right)\left(0 . 2 - X\right)$

$∴ 0 . 4 + X = 20\left(0 . 06 + {X}^{2} - 0 . 5X\right)$

$0 . 4 + X = 1 . 2 + 20{X}^{2} - 10X$

$20{X}^{2} - 11X + 0 . 8 = 0$

$X = \dfrac{11 \pm \sqrt{121 - 64}}{40}$

$= \dfrac{11 - 7 . 55}{40} ≃ 0 . 08625$

$∴ \left({PCl}_{5}\right) = 0 . 48625 ≃ 48 . 625 \times {10}^{- 2}$ or $49 \times {10}^{- 2}$

In Carius method of estimation of halogen. $0 . 45g$ of an organic compound gave $0 . 36g$ of $AgBr$. Find out the percentage of bromine in the compound.

The Carius halogen method in analytical chemistry is a method for the quantitative determination of halogens in chemical substances. A known mass of an organic compound is heated with fuming nitric acid in the presence of silver nitrate contained in a hard glass tube known as Carius tube, in a furnace.

Mass of organic compound $= 0 . 45gm$

Mass of $AgBr$ obtained $= 0 . 36gm$

$∴$Moles of $AgBr = \dfrac{0 . 36}{188}$

$∴$ Mass of Bromine $= \dfrac{0 . 36}{188} \times 80 = 0 . 1532gm$

$∴ % Br$ in compound $= \dfrac{0 . 1532}{0 . 45} \times 100 = 34 . 04 %$

30640.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Physical properties of isotopes of hydrogen are different.

Reason R : Mass difference between isotopes of hydrogen is very large.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
30640.sol:
The isotopes of hydrogen are protium, deuterium, and tritium, which have different physical properties. For example, deuterium has a higher boiling point and a lower vapor pressure than protium, while tritium is radioactive and has a much shorter half-life than the other two isotopes.

The mass difference between the isotopes of hydrogen is indeed significant, with protium having a mass of $1$ atomic mass unit (amu), deuterium having a mass of $2$ amu, and tritium having a mass of $3$ amu.

So Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

34890.subject: Mathematics
34890.text: Let $f$ be a real polynomial of degree $n$ such that $f(x) = f'(x) f''(x)$, for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f(0) = 0$, then $36\left(f'(2) + f''(2) + \int_0^2 f(x)\,dx\right)$ is equal to:
34890.sol:
Let the degree of the polynomial $f(x)$ be $n$.

The degree of $f'(x)$ is $n-1$ and the degree of $f''(x)$ is $n-2$.

Since $f(x) = f'(x) f''(x)$, equating the degrees on both sides gives:

$n = (n-1) + (n-2) \Rightarrow n = 3$

Let $f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d$.

Given $f(0) = 0$, we get $d = 0$. Thus, $f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = 3ax^2 + 2bx + c$

$f''(x) = 6ax + 2b$

Substituting these into the given equation $f(x) = f'(x) f''(x)$:

$ax^3 + bx^2 + cx = (3ax^2 + 2bx + c)(6ax + 2b)$

$ax^3 + bx^2 + cx = 18a^2x^3 + 18abx^2 + (4b^2 + 6ac)x + 2bc$

Comparing the coefficients of corresponding powers of $x$:

For $x^3$: $a = 18a^2 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{1}{18}$ (since $a \neq 0$ for a cubic polynomial)

For the constant term: $0 = 2bc$

For $x$: $c = 4b^2 + 6ac$

Substituting $a = \dfrac{1}{18}$ into the $x$ coefficient equation:

$c = 4b^2 + \dfrac{c}{3} \Rightarrow \dfrac{2c}{3} = 4b^2 \Rightarrow c = 6b^2$

From $0 = 2bc$, either $b = 0$ or $c = 0$. In either case, since $c = 6b^2$, we get $b = 0$ and $c = 0$.

Thus, the polynomial is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{18}x^3$.

Now, finding the required values:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{6}x^2 \Rightarrow f'(2) = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$f''(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}x \Rightarrow f''(2) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx = \int_0^2 \dfrac{1}{18}x^3\,dx = \dfrac{1}{18} \left[ \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right]_0^2 = \dfrac{16}{72} = \dfrac{2}{9}$

Substituting these into the given expression:

$36\left(f'(2) + f''(2) + \int_0^2 f(x)\,dx\right) = 36\left(\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9}\right)$

$= 36\left(\dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9}\right) = 36\left(\dfrac{14}{9}\right) = 4 \times 14 = 56$

Answer: $56$

37485.text:
Let $R$ be the set of real numbers
This question has Statement $-1$ and Statement $-2$. Of the four choices given after the statements, choose the one that best describes the two statements.
Statement-1 : $A=\{(x, y) \in R \times R: y-x$ is an integer $\}$ is an equivalence relation on $R$.
Statement-2 : $B=\{(x, y) \in R \times R: x=\alpha y$ for some rational number $\alpha\}$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathrm{R}$.
options:
Statement $-1$ is true, Statement $-2$ is true; Statement $-2$ is not a correct explanation for Statement $-1$

Statement $-1$ is true, Statement- 2 is false.

Statement $-1$ is false, Statement $-2$ is true.

Statement $-1$ is true, Statement $-2$ is true; Statement $-2$ is a correct explanation for Statement $-1$
37485.sol:
$\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}$ is an integer
$x-x=0$ is an integer $\Rightarrow A$ is Reflexive
$x-y$ is an integer $\Rightarrow y-x$ is an integer $\Rightarrow A$ is symmetric
$x-y, y-z$ are integers
As sum of two integers is an integer.
$\Rightarrow(x-y)+(y-z)=x-z$ is an integer
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{A}$ is transitive. Hence statement $-1$ is true.
Also $\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}}=1$ is a rational number $\Rightarrow B$ is reflexive
$\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{y}}=\alpha$ is rational $\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}$ need not be rational
i.e., $\frac{0}{1}$ is rational $\Rightarrow \frac{1}{0}$ is not rational
Hence B is not symmetric
$\Rightarrow B$ is not an equivalence relation.

38051.text:
Let the equation of the plane passing through the line
$x - 2y - z - 5 = 0 = x + y + 3z - 5$ and parallel to the line $x + y + 2z - 7 = 0 = 2x + 3y + z - 2$ be $ax + by + cz = 65$. Then the distance of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ from the plane $2x + 2y - z + 16 = 0$ is _____ .
38051.sol:
Equation of plane through the line $x - 2y - z - 5 = 0 = x + y + 3z - 5$ is

$\left(x - 2y - z - 5\right) + \lambda\left(x + y + 3z - 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ \left(1 + \lambda\right)x + \left(- 2 + \lambda\right) + \left(- 1 + 3\lambda\right)z + \left(- 5 - 5\lambda\right) = 0$

Also, this plane is parallel to the line $x + y + 2z - 7 = 0 = 2x + 3y + z - 2$, so

$\left|\begin{cases}1 + \lambda & - 2 + \lambda & - 1 + 3\lambda \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ - 5\left(1 + \lambda\right) + 3\left(\lambda - 2\right) + \left(3\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ - 5 - 5\lambda + 3\lambda - 6 + 3\lambda - 1 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 12$

So, equation of plane is

$13x + 10y + 35z = 65 . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, $a = 13, b = 10, c = 35$

So, distance of the point $\left(a, b, c\right)$ from plane $2x + 2y - z + 16 = 0$ is

$= \dfrac{26 + 20 - 35 + 16}{\sqrt{4 + 4 + 1}} = 9$ units

43999.subject: Physics
43999.text: Consider a spherical shell of radius R at temperature T. The black body radiation inside it can be considered as an ideal gas of photons with internal energy per unit volume $u = \dfrac{U}{V} ∝ {T}^{4}$ and pressure $p = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{U}{V}\right)$ . If the shell now undergoes an adiabatic expansion the relation between T and R is:
43999.sol:
$∵$ in an adiabatic process.

$Q = 0$

So by first law of thermodynamics

$Q = dU + W$

$⇒ 0 = dU + W$

$⇒ W = - dU$

$∴ W = PdV$

$⇒ PdV = - dU$ ....(i)

Given that $\dfrac{U}{V} ∝ {T}^{4} ⇒ U = kV{T}^{4}$

$⇒ dU = kd\left(V{T}^{4}\right) = K\left({T}^{4}dV + 4{T}^{3}VdT\right)$

Also, $P = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{U}{V} = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{kV{T}^{4}}{V} = \dfrac{K{T}^{4}}{3}$

Putting these values in equation (i)

$⇒ \dfrac{K{T}^{4}}{3}dV = - k\left({T}^{4}dV + 4{T}^{3}VdT\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{TdV}{3} = - TdV - 4VdT$

$⇒ \dfrac{4T}{3}dV = - 4VdT$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{dV}{V} = - \dfrac{dT}{T}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{3}ln ⁡ V = - ln ⁡ T ⇒ ln ⁡ V = ln ⁡ {T}^{- 3}$

$⇒ V{T}^{3} = \text{constant}$

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}{T}^{3} = \text{constant}$

$RT = \text{constant}$

$⇒ T ∝ \dfrac{1}{R}$

44045.subject: Physics
44045.text: $L$, $C$ and $R$ represents physical quantities inductance, capacitance and resistance respectively. The dimensional formula $ML^2 T^{-4} A^{-2}$ corresponds to __________.
44045.sol:
Dimensional formula of inductance $L$ is obtained from $E = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^2$:

$[L] = \dfrac{[E]}{[I]^2} = \dfrac{ML^2T^{-2}}{A^2} = ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2}$

Dimensional formula of capacitance $C$ is obtained from $E = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{Q^2}{C}$:

$[C] = \dfrac{[Q]^2}{[E]} = \dfrac{A^2T^2}{ML^2T^{-2}} = M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2$

Dimensional formula of resistance $R$ is obtained from $P = I^2R$:

$[R] = \dfrac{[P]}{[I]^2} = \dfrac{ML^2T^{-3}}{A^2} = ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}$

The dimensional formula of $\sqrt{LC}$ is:

$[\sqrt{LC}] = \sqrt{(ML^2T^{-2}A^{-2})(M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2)} = \sqrt{T^2} = T$

Evaluating the dimensional formula of $\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{LC}}$:

$\left[\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{LC}}\right] = \dfrac{ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}}{T} = ML^2T^{-4}A^{-2}$

This matches the given dimensional formula.

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{\sqrt{LC}}$

44382.subject: Physics
44382.text:
In an open organ pipe $
u_{3}$ and $
u_{6}$ are $3^{	ext{rd }}$ and $6^{	ext{th }}$ harmonic frequencies, respectively. If $
u_{6}-
u_{3}=2200 \mathrm{~Hz}$ then length of the pipe is $\_\_\_\_$ mm . (Take velocity of sound in air is $330 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.)
44382.sol:
For an open organ pipe, the $n$-th harmonic frequency is $f_n = n \cdot \frac{v}{2L}$.
The 3rd harmonic is $v_3 = 3 \cdot \frac{330}{2L}$ and the 6th harmonic is $v_6 = 6 \cdot \frac{330}{2L}$.
Taking the difference: $v_6 - v_3 = (6-3) \cdot \frac{330}{2L} = 3 \cdot \frac{330}{2L} = 2200$.
Solving for $L$: $L = \frac{3 \times 330}{2 \times 2200} = \frac{990}{4400} = 0.225$ m = 225 mm.

49664.sol:
Given vectors,\[

\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\lambda \hat{j}+2 \hat{k} \rightarrow(1) \\

\Rightarrow(\hat{i}+\lambda \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \cdot(\mu \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})=0 \\

\end{array}$

 \begin{array}{l}

\Rightarrow \lambda^{2}+3=4+\lambda^{2}-4 \lambda \\
\text{ So, } \lambda=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow \mu=2-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{7}{4}
\end{array}$\]\[
$\text{ Hence }(\lambda, \mu)=  \left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{7}{4}\right)\]

\Rightarrow & 1+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{u}{f} \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{3}{2}=\frac{0.72}{f} \\
\text{ or } \quad & f=\frac{0.72 \times 2}{3}=0.16 \mathrm{ m}
\end{array}$
As the object is moved by 0.04 $\mathrm{ m}$ towards the lens, the new
$ u_{1}=0.72-0.04=0.68 \mathrm{ m}
Again real image is formed
So, 1+\frac{1}{m}=\frac{u_{1}}{f}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{m}=\frac{0.04}{0.16}\Rightarrow \quad$ m=4

51775.text: Suppose $A$~is $3 \times 3$~matrix consisting of integer entries that are chosen at random from the set $\left\{- 1000, - 999, \ldots 999, 1000\right\} .$ Let $P$ be the probability that either $A^{2} = - I or A$ is diagonal, where $I$ is the $3 \times 3$ identity matrix. Then,
51775.sol:
We have, $A$ is $3 \times 3$~matrix consisting of integer entries from $\left\{- 1000, - 999, \ldots 999, 1000\right\}$

Total entries $= 2001$

Total number of outcomes $= \left(2001\right)9$

Given, $A^{2} = - I, A = - A^{- 1}$ (which is not~possible)

$A$ is diagonal matrix.

$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & a & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & a\end{cases}\right]$

Total number of favourable outcomes

$= \left(2001\right)3$

Required probability

$= \dfrac{\left(2001\right)3}{\left(2001\right)9}\left(2001\right)- 6 = \left(2000 + 1\right)- 6$

$p = \left(2000\right)- 6\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2000}\right)- 6$

$P = \dfrac{1}{{2}^{6} \times {10}^{18}}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2000}\right)- 6$

So, $\dfrac{Imin}{I0} = \dfrac{k\piR^{2} \times 9999}{k\piR^{2} \times 10000}$

55977.subject: Chemistry
55977.text: Half life of a first order reaction is $900$ second. If initial concentration of reactant is $0.08\,\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ find concentration that remains after $35$ minute ?
55977.sol:
Given $t_{1/2} = 900$ s and $t = 35$ min $= 35 \times 60 = 2100$ s.

Number of half-lives $n = \dfrac{t}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{2100}{900} = \dfrac{7}{3}$.

For a first order reaction, the concentration remaining after $n$ half-lives is given by:

$[A] = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2^n}$

Substituting the given values:

$[A] = \dfrac{0.08}{2^{7/3}}$

$[A] = \dfrac{0.08}{4 \times 2^{1/3}}$

Since $2^{1/3} \approx 1.26$:

$[A] \approx \dfrac{0.08}{4 \times 1.26} = \dfrac{0.08}{5.04} \approx 0.0159 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$

Answer: $0.0159\,\text{mol dm}^{-3}$

56664.subject: Chemistry
56664.text: $Identify the element having highest ionisation enthalpy  \left(\mathrm{IE}_1\right) from following.$
56664.sol:
The first ionization enthalpy represents the energy needed to remove the most loosely bound electron from a neutral gaseous atom. Lanthanides exhibit a general increasing trend due to the lanthanide contraction, which raises the effective nuclear charge with atomic number. However, deviations occur when stable electronic configurations (half-filled or fully-filled f-orbitals) are present.

Relevant electronic configurations include La: $[\text{Xe}]\ 5d^1\ 6s^2$, Ce: $[\text{Xe}]\ 4f^1\ 5d^1\ 6s^2$, Gd: $[\text{Xe}]\ 4f^7\ 5d^1\ 6s^2$ (half-filled $4f^7$), and Yb: $[\text{Xe}]\ 4f^{14}\ 6s^2$ (fully-filled $4f^{14}$).

Ytterbium, approaching the series end, experiences a notably high effective nuclear charge on its $6s$ electrons due to cumulative lanthide contraction. Removing an electron from $[\text{Xe}]\ 4f^{14}\ 6s^2$ to form the stable $[\text{Xe}]\ 4f^{14}\ 6s^1$ requires substantial energy.

Measured values confirm this: La ($538.1\,\text{kJ/mol}$), Ce ($534.4\,\text{kJ/mol}$), Gd ($593.4\,\text{kJ/mol}$), Yb ($603.9\,\text{kJ/mol}$). Yb has the highest first ionization enthalpy.

With $E^{}^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = 0.5\text{ V}$,
$\Delta G^{}^{\circ} = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.5 = -96500\text{ J}$.

Converting to kilojoules:

57169.text: According to carbinol system tert butyl alcohol is named as,
57169.sol:
In the carbinol system, alcohols are named as derivatives of methanol by replacing hydrogen atoms on the methyl group with substituents.

Tert-butyl alcohol has the formula $(CH_3)_3C\text{--}OH$, where the carbinol carbon is bonded to three methyl groups. This corresponds to trimethyl carbinol.

The alternatives correspond to different structures: methyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2OH$), ethyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2CH_2OH$), and propyl carbinol (CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2OH$).

The correct carbinol system name is therefore trimethyl carbinol.

$

57369.subject: Chemistry
57369.text: Which among the following is benzylic halide?
57369.sol:
A benzylic halide features a halogen atom bonded to an $\mathrm{sp}^3$-hybridized benzylic carbon, which is the carbon attached directly to an aromatic ring.

In $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{X}$, the halogen is bonded to an $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbon that is benzylic. This matches the definition.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{X}$ is an aryl halide, with halogen attached to $\mathrm{sp}^2$ aromatic carbon.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}{=}\mathrm{CH}{-}\mathrm{X}$ is a vinylic halide, with halogen on $\mathrm{sp}^2$ vinylic carbon.

$\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{CH}_2{-}\mathrm{X}$ has a halogen on a non-benzylic $\mathrm{sp}^3$ carbon.

The benzylic halide is $\boxed{A}$.

58867.text: Identify the defect that develops when the ratio of number of cations to anions become different from that indicated by its chemical formula.
58867.sol:
The defect that alters the cation-anion ratio from the stoichiometric formula is a nonstoichiometric defect. Schottky defects preserve stoichiometry through balanced vacancies, interstitial defects may or may not affect ratios depending on type, and substitutional impurities do not inherently disrupt the original compound's stoichiometric proportion.

Nonstoichiometric defects explicitly create excess metal (via anion vacancies or interstitial cations) or metal deficiency (via cation vacancies), directly changing the $\frac{\text{cations}}{\text{anions}}$ ratio. These deviations are characteristic of compounds exhibiting variable composition.

The correct answer is $\boxed{D}$.

For $0.05\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{MgSO}_4$, dissociation gives $i = 2$ and $i \cdot m = 2 \times 0.05 = 0.1$.

Compared to values of $0.2$, $0.16$, and $0.3$ for options A, C, and D respectively, $0.1$ is the lowest.

60952.text:
If the function $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous in $0 \leq x \leq \pi$, then the value of $2 a+3 b$ is where
$f(x)= \begin{cases}x+a \sqrt{2} \sin x & \text{ if } 0 \leq x < \frac{\pi}{4} \\ 2 x \cot x+b & \text{ if } \frac{\pi}{4} \leq x \leq \frac{\pi}{2} \\ a \cos 2 x-b \sin x & \text{ if } \frac{\pi}{2} < x \leq \pi\end{cases}$
60952.sol:
$\mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous in $0 \leq x \leq \pi\therefore \quad \mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$.
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{4}} \mathrm{f}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{4}} \mathrm{f}(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}^{-}}(x+\mathrm{a} \sqrt{2} \sin x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{4}}(2 x \cot x+\mathrm{b}) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}+\mathrm{a} \sqrt{2} \times \sin \frac{\pi}{4}=2 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \cot \frac{\pi}{4}+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}+\mathrm{a}=\frac{\pi}{2}+\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b}=\frac{\pi}{4}... (i)
\end{aligned}$
Also, $\mathrm{f}(x)$ is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad & \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} \mathrm{f}(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}} \mathrm{f}(x) \\
& \Rightarrow \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}}(2 x \cot x+\mathrm{b})=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}}(\mathrm{a} \cos 2 x-\mathrm{b} \sin x) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 \times \frac{\pi}{2} \times \cot \frac{\pi}{2}+\mathrm{b}=\mathrm{a} \cos \left(2 \times \frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\mathrm{b} \sin \frac{\pi}{2} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=-\mathrm{a}-\mathrm{b} \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=-2 \mathrm{ b}
\end{aligned}$
Substituting $a=-2 b$ in equation (i), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& -2 b-b=\frac{\pi}{4} \\
& \Rightarrow b=\frac{-\pi}{12} \\
& \Rightarrow a=-2 \times \frac{-\pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{6}
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\begin{aligned} 2 \mathrm{a}+3 \mathrm{ b} & =2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+3\left(\frac{-\pi}{12}\right) \\ & =\frac{\pi}{3}-\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{12}\end{aligned}$

61673.text: If $x = \sin(t), y = \cos(pt)$, then $(1 - x^2)\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} - x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = $
61673.sol:
Given $x = \sin(t)$ and $y = \cos(pt)$

$t = \sin^{-1}(x)$

Substituting $t$ in $y$:

$y = \cos(p \sin^{-1}(x))$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\sin(p \sin^{-1}(x)) \cdot \dfrac{p}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

$\sqrt{1 - x^2} \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -p \sin(p \sin^{-1}(x))$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$:

$\sqrt{1 - x^2} \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} \left( \dfrac{-x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} \right) = -p \cos(p \sin^{-1}(x)) \cdot \dfrac{p}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

Multiplying the entire equation by $\sqrt{1 - x^2}$:

$(1 - x^2) \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -p^2 \cos(p \sin^{-1}(x))$

Since $y = \cos(p \sin^{-1}(x))$, we get:

$(1 - x^2) \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -p^2 y$

Answer: $-p^2 y$

66335.subject: Physics
66335.text: The current (I) drawn from the battery in the given circuit is
66335.sol:
Equivalent resistance calculation begins with recognizing the balanced Wheatstone bridge configuration. The resistances satisfy the balance condition $\frac{R_{AB}}{R_{AC}} = \frac{R_{BD}}{R_{CD}}$, where $\frac{5\,\Omega}{10\,\Omega} = \frac{10\,\Omega}{20\,\Omega}$, confirming no current flows through the $10\,\Omega$ resistor between B and C.

Removing this resistor yields two parallel branches: one with $R_1 = R_{AB} + R_{BD} = 15\,\Omega$ (A-B-D) and another with $R_2 = R_{AC} + R_{CD} = 30\,\Omega$ (A-C-D). The total equivalent resistance is $R_{eq} = \frac{R_1 \times R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = 10\,\Omega$.

Applying Ohm's law with battery voltage $V = 5\,V$ gives the current $I = \frac{V}{R_{eq}} = 0.5\,A$.

Final answer: $\boxed{0.5\text{ A}}$

67556.text: Which one of the following person is in an inertial frame of reference?
options: A person (man) in a train which is slowing down to stop.
A person (child) revolving in a merry-go-round.
A person (driver) in a bus which is moving with constant velocity.
A person (pilot) in an aeroplane which is taking off.
67556.sol:
An inertial frame of reference is defined as one moving with constant velocity (including rest), where Newton's first law holds true. Frames undergoing acceleration are non-inertial.

A person on a train slowing down experiences deceleration, indicating a non-inertial frame.

Circular motion on a merry-go-round involves centripetal acceleration, also non-inertial.

A bus moving at constant velocity has zero acceleration, making it an inertial frame.

An airplane taking off accelerates during departure, resulting in a non-inertial frame.

Only the bus driver moving at constant velocity occupies an inertial frame:

69936.subject: Physics
69936.text: The relation between efficiency $(\eta)$ of Carnot engine and coefficient of performance (\eta_1$ ) of refrigerator is$
69936.sol:
Relating efficiency and coefficient of performance

The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between reservoirs at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ is given by $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_2}{T_1}$, from which we obtain $\frac{T_2}{T_1} = 1 - \eta$.

The coefficient of performance for a refrigerator operating between the same reservoirs is $\eta_1 = \frac{T_2}{T_1 - T_2}$. Dividing numerator and denominator by $T_1$ gives $\eta_1 = \frac{T_2/T_1}{1 - T_2/T_1}$.

Substituting $T_2/T_1 = 1 - \eta$ yields $\eta_1 = \frac{1 - \eta}{1 - (1 - \eta)} = \frac{1 - \eta}{\eta}$.

Solving for $\eta$ gives $\eta_1\eta = 1 - \eta$, then $\eta(\eta_1 + 1) = 1$, resulting in $\eta = \frac{1}{\eta_1 + 1}$.

Final answer: $\boxed{A}$

71466.subject: Biology
71466.text:
Given below are two statements related to Kreb's cycle.
Statement (I): There are four steps of oxidation in Kreb's cycle, catalyzed by dehydrogenases using $\text{NAD}^+$ or $\text{FAD}^+$ as the coenzyme.
Statement (II): Two molecules of GTP are produced for every molecule of citric acid oxidized.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are correct.
Both Statement (I) and Statement (II) are incorrect.
Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.
Statement (I) is incorrect but Statement (II) is correct.
71466.sol:
In the Krebs cycle, there are four oxidation steps where hydrogen atoms are removed and transferred to coenzymes. These steps are catalyzed by dehydrogenases:
1. Isocitrate to $\alpha$-ketoglutarate ($\text{NAD}^+ \rightarrow \text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$)
2. $\alpha$-ketoglutarate to succinyl-CoA ($\text{NAD}^+ \rightarrow \text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$)
3. Succinate to fumarate ($\text{FAD} \rightarrow \text{FADH}_2$)
4. Malate to oxaloacetate ($\text{NAD}^+ \rightarrow \text{NADH} + \text{H}^+$)
Thus, Statement (I) is correct.

During the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate, one molecule of GTP is synthesized through substrate-level phosphorylation. Since one molecule of citric acid undergoes one turn of the Krebs cycle, only one molecule of GTP is produced per molecule of citric acid oxidized, not two. Thus, Statement (II) is incorrect.

Therefore, Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

Answer: Statement (I) is correct but Statement (II) is incorrect.

71513.subject: Biology
71513.text: Starting from the innermost part, the correct sequence of parts in an angiospermic ovule is
71513.sol:
The innermost part of an angiospermic ovule is the egg cell, which is the female gamete.

The egg cell is situated within the embryo sac, also known as the female gametophyte.

The embryo sac is enclosed by a mass of parenchymatous cells called the nucellus, which provides nourishment.

The nucellus is surrounded and protected by one or two outer layers known as the integuments.

Thus, the correct sequence from the innermost part to the outermost part is: Egg, embryo sac, nucellus, integument.

Answer: Egg, embryo sac, nucellus, integument

72157.subject: Physics
72157.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of the free electron is '$\lambda$' and has a kinetic energy $E_k$. If the kinetic energy of the free electron is made double, the new de-Broglie wavelength is '$\lambda_1$'. If $\lambda_1 = x\,\lambda$, then the value of $x$ is
72157.sol:
The de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ of an electron with kinetic energy $E_k$ is given by

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE_k}}$

When the kinetic energy is doubled, the new kinetic energy is $E_k' = 2E_k$. The new de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_1$ becomes

$\lambda_1 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(2E_k)}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE_k}}$

$\lambda_1 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \lambda$

Given $\lambda_1 = x \lambda$, comparing the two expressions gives

$x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The sequence of the middle four sentences has been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Sentence S1 introduces the inauguration of the South African Constitution. Sentence P logically follows S1 as it refers to the creation and promulgation of the Constitution mentioned in S1 using the pronoun 'Its'.

Sentence Q shifts the focus to a specific part of the Constitution, introducing the 'Bill of Rights'.

Sentence S must follow Q as it elaborates on the 'Bill of Rights' introduced in Q, stating that it grants an extensive range of rights.

Sentence R follows S by providing specific details and examples of the extensive rights mentioned in S, specifically forbidding various forms of discrimination.

Finally, S6 concludes the passage by stating how these rights are enforced by a special constitutional court.

Thus, the correct logical sequence is PQSR.

76574.subject: Mathematics
76574.text:
Passage: Let $u$ be a positive integer and $f$ be a real number lying between $0 and 1$. Further, $\left(\sqrt{2}+1\right)^{10}=u+f$ and $\left(\sqrt{2}-1\right)^{10}=v$.

Question: What is the value of $u$ ?
76574.sol:
Given $(\sqrt{2}+1)^{10} = u + f$ and $(\sqrt{2}-1)^{10} = v$.

Adding the two equations:

$u + f + v = (\sqrt{2}+1)^{10} + (\sqrt{2}-1)^{10}$

Using the binomial expansion $(x+y)^n + (x-y)^n = 2 [^{n}C_{0} x^n + ^{n}C_{2} x^{n-2} y^2 + \dots]$:

$u + f + v = 2 [^{10}C_{0}(\sqrt{2})^{10} + ^{10}C_{2}(\sqrt{2})^8 + ^{10}C_{4}(\sqrt{2})^6 + ^{10}C_{6}(\sqrt{2})^4 + ^{10}C_{8}(\sqrt{2})^2 + ^{10}C_{10}]$

$u + f + v = 2 [1(32) + 45(16) + 210(8) + 210(4) + 45(2) + 1(1)]$

$u + f + v = 2 [32 + 720 + 1680 + 840 + 90 + 1]$

$u + f + v = 2 [3363] = 6726$

Since $0 < \sqrt{2}-1 < 1$, we have $0 < (\sqrt{2}-1)^{10} < 1$, which means $0 < v < 1$.

We are given $0 < f < 1$. Adding these inequalities gives $0 < f + v < 2$.

Since $u$ and $6726$ are integers, $f + v$ must be an integer. The only integer strictly between $0$ and $2$ is $1$.

Therefore, $f + v = 1$.

Substituting this back into the equation:

$u + 1 = 6726$

$u = 6725$

Answer: $6725$

77404.subject: Mathematics
77404.text:
Consider the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{27\left(\mathrmx^{2 / 3}-\mathrm{x}\right)}{4}$
How many solutions does the function $\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=1$ have?
77404.sol:
$\begin{aligned} f(x) & =\frac{27}{4}\left(x^{2 / 3}-x\right) \\ & =\frac{27}{4}\left(\left(x^2\right)^{1 / 3}-x\right)\end{aligned}$ For $f(x)=1\begin{aligned} & \frac{27}{4}\left(\left(x^2\right)^{1 / 3}-x\right)=1 \\ & \left(x^{1 / 3}\right)^2-x=\frac{4}{27} \end{aligned}$ Put $x^{1 / 3}=yx=y^3\begin{aligned} & y^2-y^3=\frac{4}{27} \\ & \Rightarrow y^3-y^2+\frac{4}{27}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow 27 y^3-27 y^2+4=0 \end{aligned}$ This is a cubic equation. If we put $y=-\frac{1}{3}$ then $(3 y+1)=0$ is a factor of cubic equation.
$\begin{aligned} & (3 y+1)\left(9 y^2-12 y+4\right)=0 \\ & (3 y+1)(3 y-2)^2=0 \end{aligned}$ Hence $y=-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{3}$ Thus $f(x)=1$ has two solutions.

84500.subject: Zoology
84500.text: Motile zygote of Plasmodium occurs in
84500.sol: When female Anopheles sucks the blood of an infected person, the gametocytes of Plasmodium are picked up by the mosquito. Now sexual reproduction of Plasmodium occurs inside mosquito. The outer envelope of gametocyte is dissolved and its contents are liberated into the cavity of gut. These contents then undergo gametogony, i.e., formation of microgametes and macroagamete. The nuclei of both fuse and a synkaryon or zygote is formed. This zygote is motionless and spherical for sometime but becomes motile, elongated and vermiform very soon. Now, it is called vermicule or ookinete. Ookinete pierces the stomach wall and forms a cyst (oocyst) on its outer surface which has about 10000 sporozoites. The latter pass into salivary glands of the mosquito.

85442.subject: Zoology
85442.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
85442.text:
Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence.
A. Digestion of cell walls.
B. Isolation of naked protoplasts.
C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast.
D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieties of plants.
E. Growing of hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
85442.sol:
Somatic hybridisation involves the fusion of protoplasts of two different plant varieties to produce a hybrid plant.

The correct sequence of steps is as follows:

First, single cells are isolated from two different varieties of plants (Step D).

Next, the cell walls of these isolated cells are digested using enzymes such as cellulase and pectinase (Step A).

This digestion results in the isolation of naked protoplasts, which are cells without cell walls (Step B).

The isolated naked protoplasts from the two different varieties are then fused together, often using chemicals like PEG or electrical stimulation, to get a hybrid protoplast (Step C).

Finally, the hybrid protoplast is cultured and grown to form a new plant (Step E).

Thus, the correct sequence is D, A, B, C, E.

Answer: D, A, B, C, E

92786.text: In the given circuit, the voltmeter reading is $4.5V$. Assuming that the voltmeter is ideal, current through $12Ω$ resistance is -
92786.sol:
The voltmeter is ideal so it doesn't draw any current from the circuit.
Potential difference across $9Ω$ resistance = $4.5V$ (given)

So the current in the $9Ω$ resistance = $\dfrac{4.5}{9} = 0.5A$

i.e., ${I}_{1}^{′} = 0.5A$

The same current ${I}_{1}^{′}$ passes through $3Ω$. The resistors $9Ω$ and $3Ω$ are in series and their equivalent, i.e., $12Ω$ is in parallel with $6Ω$ between $A$ and $B$ . Dividing the current in the inverse ratio of resistances between $A$ and $B$ ,

$\dfrac{{I}_{1}^{′}}{{I}_{1}^{′′}} = \dfrac{6}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

${I}_{1}^{′′} = 2{I}_{1}^{′} = 2 \times 0.5 = 1A$

and ${I}_{1} = {I}_{1}^{′} + {I}_{1}^{′′} = 0.5 + 1 = 1.5A$

at junction $C, {I}_{1}$ divides into three parts. Since the resistances $10Ω, 12Ω, 15Ω$ are in parallel between $C$ and $D$ , current will distribute in the inverse ratio of resistances.

$∴ {I}_{2}^{′}: {I}_{2}^{′′}: {I}_{2}^{′′′} = \dfrac{1}{10}: \dfrac{1}{12}: \dfrac{1}{15}$

$= 6: 5: 4$

${I}_{2}^{′} = \dfrac{5}{15} \times 1.5 = 0.5A$

So ${I}_{2}^{′} = 6k, {I}_{2}^{′′} = 5k, {I}_{2}^{′′′} = 4k$

( $k$ being a constant of proportionality)

and ${I}_{1} = {I}_{2}^{′} + {I}_{2}^{′′} + {I}_{2}^{′′′} = 15k$

but ${I}_{1} = 1.5A$

$∴ 15k = 1.5$

or $k = 0.1$

so ${I}_{2}^{′′} = 5k = 0.5A$

Thus current through $12Ω$ resistance is $0.5A$

${W}_{ab} = {nRT}_{b} ln \dfrac{2 {V}_{0}}{{V}_{0}} = 2 \text{R} \times 5 0 0 ln 2 = 1 0 0 0 R ln 2$

and ${W}_{cd} = {nRT}_{c} ln \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2 {V}_{0}} = 2 \text{R} \times 3 0 0 ln \dfrac{1}{2} = - 6 0 0 R ln 2$

There is no volume change from b to c and from d to a, so

The work done in the complete cycle

$\text{W} = {W}_{ab} + {W}_{bc} + {W}_{cd} + {W}_{da}$

94867.text: In a special arrangement of Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between the slits $d$ is twice the distance between the screen and the slits $D$, i.e $d = 2D$. 94867.sol:
From diagram as provided in question, $OP = x$
$CO = D$
${S}_{1}C = {S}_{2}C = D{T}_{1}P = {T}_{1}O - OP = D - x$
${T}_{2}P = {T}_{2}O + OP = D + x$
Now, ${S}_{1}p = \sqrt{{\left({S}_{1}{T}_{1}\right)}^{2} + {\left({T}_{1}P\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}}$

${S}_{2}P = \sqrt{{\left({S}_{2}{T}_{2}\right)}^{2} + {\left({T}_{2}P\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}}$

For fist minimum to occur,

Path difference

${S}_{2}P - {S}_{1}P = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

The first minimum falls at a distance $D$ from the centre, i.e., $x = D$

$\left[{D}^{2} + 4{D}^{2}\right]\dfrac{1}{2} - D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$∴ D\left(\sqrt{5} - 1\right) = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\left(2 . 24 - 1\right)} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2 . 48}$

95628.text: Which one of the following statements is correct about Phycomycetes?
options: The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes.
95628.sol: In the members of Phycomycetes, the mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in the sporangium. A zygospore is formed by the fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (the bread mould mentioned earlier), and Albugo (the parasitic fungi on mustard).

100903.subject: Physics
100903.text: A small ball is dropped from a height of $20\text{ m}$ above a horizontal floor. After striking the floor, it rebounds to a maximum height of $5\text{ m}$. The percentage of kinetic energy lost by the ball during the collision with the floor is:
100903.sol:
Let the mass of the ball be $m$.

The kinetic energy of the ball just before striking the floor is equal to its initial potential energy:
$K_{i} = mgh_{i} = mg(20)$

The kinetic energy of the ball just after the rebound is equal to the potential energy at its maximum rebound height:
$K_{f} = mgh_{f} = mg(5)$

The loss in kinetic energy during the collision is:
$\Delta K = K_{i} - K_{f} = 20mg - 5mg = 15mg$

The percentage loss of kinetic energy is:
$\text{Percentage loss} = \left( \dfrac{\Delta K}{K_{i}} \right) \times 100$
$\text{Percentage loss} = \left( \dfrac{15mg}{20mg} \right) \times 100 = 75\%$

Answer: $75\%$

101558.subject: Physics
101558.text:
Read the following statements regarding the elastic properties of materials:
Statement I: Young's modulus is defined as the ratio of tensile or compressive stress to the longitudinal strain.
Statement II: Bulk modulus is defined as the ratio of hydraulic stress to the corresponding volumetric strain.
Statement III: Compressibility is defined as the fractional decrease in volume per unit increase in pressure.
Statement IV: Poisson's ratio is defined as the ratio of longitudinal strain to lateral strain.

How many of the given statements are correct?
101558.sol:
Statement I is correct: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal (tensile or compressive) stress to longitudinal strain.

Statement II is correct: Bulk modulus is the ratio of hydraulic stress to volumetric strain.

Statement III is correct: Compressibility is the reciprocal of bulk modulus, which mathematically represents the fractional decrease in volume per unit increase in pressure ($k = -\dfrac{1}{\Delta P}\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}$).

Statement IV is incorrect: Poisson's ratio is defined as the ratio of lateral strain to longitudinal strain, not the other way around.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Only three

103294.text: A cell of emf $1.5 \text{ V}$ is connected across an external resistor of $4 \Omega$. If the terminal potential difference measured across the cell is $1.2 \text{ V}$, the internal resistance of the cell is:
103294.sol:
The current $i$ flowing through the external resistor is given by Ohm's law:
$i = \dfrac{V}{R}$
$i = \dfrac{1.2}{4} = 0.3 \text{ A}$

The terminal potential difference of a discharging cell is related to its emf and internal resistance by:
$V = E - ir$

Rearranging for the internal resistance $r$:
$ir = E - V$
$r = \dfrac{E - V}{i}$
$r = \dfrac{1.5 - 1.2}{0.3} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.3} = 1.0 \Omega$

Answer: $1.0 \Omega$

103333.subject: Physics
103333.text: An electric bulb is rated $100$ W, $200$ V. When it is connected across a fluctuating supply line, the power dissipated by the bulb is found to be $64$ W. Assuming the resistance of the bulb remains constant, what is the actual line voltage applied to the bulb?
103333.sol:
The resistance of the bulb is constant and is related to its rated values by $R = \dfrac{V_{\text{rated}}^2}{P_{\text{rated}}}$.

The actual power consumed when connected to the line is $P_{\text{actual}} = \dfrac{V_{\text{actual}}^2}{R}$.

Dividing the two equations, we get:
$\dfrac{P_{\text{actual}}}{P_{\text{rated}}} = \left( \dfrac{V_{\text{actual}}}{V_{\text{rated}}} \right)^2$

Substituting the given values:
$\dfrac{64}{100} = \left( \dfrac{V_{\text{actual}}}{200} \right)^2$

Taking the square root on both sides:
$\dfrac{8}{10} = \dfrac{V_{\text{actual}}}{200}$

$V_{\text{actual}} = 200 \times 0.8 = 160$ V.

Answer: $160$ V

103937.subject: Physics
103937.text: Two coaxial circular coils, $P$ and $Q$, are placed near each other. An observer looks along their common axis such that coil $P$ is closer to them. Coil $P$ is connected to a battery through a switch, while coil $Q$ is a closed metallic loop. When the switch is just closed, the current in coil $P$ is clockwise as seen by the observer. What will be the direction of the induced current in coil $Q$ as seen by the same observer, and what is the nature of the magnetic force between the two coils?
103937.sol:
When the switch is closed, the current in coil $P$ increases from zero, causing an increasing magnetic flux through coil $Q$.

As seen by the observer, the current in $P$ is clockwise, so the magnetic field produced by $P$ points away from the observer (towards $Q$).

According to Lenz's law, the induced current in $Q$ will oppose this increase in flux. Therefore, coil $Q$ will produce a magnetic field pointing towards the observer.

For the magnetic field of $Q$ to point towards the observer, the induced current in $Q$ must be anti-clockwise as seen by the observer.

Since the two coils carry currents in opposite directions (clockwise and anti-clockwise), they will repel each other. Alternatively, the face of $P$ towards $Q$ acts as a North pole, and to oppose the increasing flux, the face of $Q$ towards $P$ also becomes a North pole, resulting in repulsion.

Answer: Anti-clockwise, repulsive force

104854.subject: Physics
104854.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, for a given impact parameter and incident kinetic energy, a target nucleus with a larger atomic number ($Z$) will scatter an $\alpha$-particle by a larger angle.
Reason (R): The Coulomb repulsive force between the $\alpha$-particle and the target nucleus is inversely proportional to the atomic number of the target nucleus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
104854.sol:
The impact parameter $b$ is given by the relation $b = \dfrac{Z e^2 \cot(\theta/2)}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 K}$.

For a fixed impact parameter $b$ and incident kinetic energy $K$, the product $Z \cot(\theta/2)$ is constant. If the atomic number $Z$ increases, $\cot(\theta/2)$ must decrease. Since $\cot(\theta/2)$ is a decreasing function for angles between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, the scattering angle $\theta$ must increase. Thus, the Assertion (A) is true.

The Coulomb repulsive force between an $\alpha$-particle (charge $2e$) and a nucleus (charge $Ze$) is $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{(2e)(Ze)}{r^2}$. This force is directly proportional to the atomic number $Z$, not inversely proportional. Thus, the Reason (R) is false.

Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

104885.subject: Physics
104885.text: In a muonic hydrogen atom, a muon (which has a mass $200$ times that of an electron) replaces the electron and revolves around the proton. If the muon and a normal electron are moving with the exact same orbital speed in their respective hydrogenic atoms, what is the ratio of the radius of the muon's orbit to the radius of the normal electron's orbit ($r_{\mu} : r_e$)?
104885.sol:
For a particle of mass $m$ and charge $e$ revolving around a proton with speed $v$ in an orbit of radius $r$, the centripetal force is provided by the electrostatic force of attraction.

$\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r^2}$

Rearranging for the radius $r$:

$r = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{mv^2}$

For a fixed orbital speed $v$, the radius $r$ is inversely proportional to the mass $m$ of the revolving particle ($r \propto \dfrac{1}{m}$).

Therefore, the ratio of the radii is:

$\dfrac{r_{\mu}}{r_e} = \dfrac{m_e}{m_{\mu}} = \dfrac{m_e}{200 m_e} = \dfrac{1}{200}$

The ratio is $1 : 200$.

Answer: $1 : 200$

105407.text: What maximum frequency can be reflected from ionosphere?
105407.sol: The ionosphere extends from a height of 80 km to 300 km . The refractive index of ionosphere is less than its free space value. That is, it behaves as a rarer medium. As we go deep into the ionosphere, the refractive index keeps on decreasing. The bending of beam (away from the normal) will continue till it reaches critical angle after which it will be reflected back. 105901.text:
An impure sample of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ weighing $1.16\text{ g}$ is completely neutralized by $40\text{ mL}$ of a $0.5\text{ M HCl}$ solution. What is the percentage purity of the $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ sample?

(Given molar mass of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 = 58\text{ g mol}^{-1}$)
105901.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the neutralization reaction is:
$\text{Mg(OH)}_2(\text{s}) + 2\text{HCl}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$

Number of moles of $\text{HCl}$ used $= \text{Molarity} \times \text{Volume in L}$
$= 0.5\text{ M} \times 0.040\text{ L} = 0.02\text{ mol}$

From the balanced equation, $2\text{ moles}$ of $\text{HCl}$ neutralize $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.
Therefore, moles of pure $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ present $= \dfrac{0.02}{2} = 0.01\text{ mol}$.

Mass of pure $\text{Mg(OH)}_2 = 0.01\text{ mol} \times 58\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.58\text{ g}$.

The percentage purity of the sample is given by:
$\text{Percentage purity} = \dfrac{\text{Mass of pure substance}}{\text{Total mass of sample}} \times 100$
$\text{Percentage purity} = \dfrac{0.58\text{ g}}{1.16\text{ g}} \times 100 = 50\%$.

Answer: $50\%$

105918.subject: Chemistry
105918.text: A container holds a sample of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas and a sample of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ gas. If both samples contain the exact same total number of atoms, what is the ratio of the mass of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ to the mass of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ in the container?
105918.sol:
Let the total number of atoms in each sample be $x$.

The atomicity of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is 3 (1 S + 2 O). The number of moles of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is $\dfrac{x}{3 N_A}$.

The atomicity of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is 5 (1 C + 4 H). The number of moles of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is $\dfrac{x}{5 N_A}$.

The ratio of their moles is $n(\mathrm{SO_2}) : n(\mathrm{CH_4}) = \dfrac{1}{3} : \dfrac{1}{5} = 5 : 3$.

The molar mass of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is $32 + 2(16) = 64\text{ g/mol}$.
The molar mass of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ is $12 + 4(1) = 16\text{ g/mol}$.

The ratio of their masses is $\dfrac{n(\mathrm{SO_2}) \times M(\mathrm{SO_2})}{n(\mathrm{CH_4}) \times M(\mathrm{CH_4})} = \dfrac{5 \times 64}{3 \times 16} = \dfrac{320}{48} = \dfrac{20}{3}$.

Thus, the mass ratio is $20 : 3$.

Answer: $20 : 3$

Dipole moment is a vector quantity and by convention it is depicted by a small arrow with tail on the negative centre and head pointing towards the positive centre. 108643.subject: Chemistry
108643.text:
Match List-I with List-II for the relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) at constant temperature.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Relationship)
(A) $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$(I) $\Delta H = \Delta U - 2RT$
(B) $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g})$(II) $\Delta H = \Delta U - RT$
(C) $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$(III) $\Delta H = \Delta U$
(D) $2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$(IV) $\Delta H = \Delta U + RT$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
108643.sol:
The relationship between enthalpy change and internal energy change is given by $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$, where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gaseous species.

For reaction (A): $\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HI}(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0$
Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U$
Matches with (III).

For reaction (B): $\mathrm{PCl}_5(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{PCl}_3(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = (1 + 1) - 1 = +1$
Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U + RT$
Matches with (IV).

For reaction (C): $\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 3\mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (1 + 3) = -2$
Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U - 2RT$
Matches with (I).

For reaction (D): $2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g})$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - (2 + 1) = -1$
Therefore, $\Delta H = \Delta U - RT$
Matches with (II).

The correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

113765.text:
Consider following statement :-
(a) Molarity depends on temperature
(b) Molality does not depend on temperature
(c) On dilution, concentration of solution will be increased
(d) Sum of the mole fraction of all the components present in a solution are unity
Which statements are correct?
options: Statement \(A\) and \(B\) are correct, \(C\) and \(D\) are incorrect
Statement \(A, B, C\) are correct, \(D\) are incorrect
Only statement \(A\) is correct, \(B, C, D\) are incorrect
113765.sol:
(a) Molarity depends on temperature.
- This statement is correct. Molarity is defined as moles of solute per liter of solution, and since volume can change with temperature, molarity can vary with temperature.
(b) Molality does not depend on temperature.
- This statement is correct. Molality is defined as moles of solute per kilogram of solvent, and this measurement is not affected by temperature, as mass does not change with temperature.
(c) On dilution, the concentration of solution will be increased.
- This statement is not correct. Dilution refers to adding more solvent, which decreases the concentration of the solute in the solution.
(d) The sum of the mole fractions of all the components present in a solution is unity.
- This statement is correct. The sum of mole fractions in a solution always equals one.

113876.subject: Chemistry
113876.text: An ideal binary solution is prepared by mixing two volatile liquids, A and B. The vapour pressure of pure liquid A is $150\text{ torr}$ and that of pure liquid B is $300\text{ torr}$ at a certain temperature. If the total vapour pressure of the solution at the same temperature is $210\text{ torr}$, what is the mole fraction of component A in the liquid mixture?
113876.sol:
According to Raoult's Law, the total vapour pressure of an ideal binary solution is given by:
$P_{\text{total}} = X_{\text{A}}P_{\text{A}}^{\circ} + X_{\text{B}}P_{\text{B}}^{\circ}$

Since $X_{\text{A}} + X_{\text{B}} = 1$, we can write this in terms of $X_{\text{A}}$:
$P_{\text{total}} = X_{\text{A}}P_{\text{A}}^{\circ} + (1 - X_{\text{A}})P_{\text{B}}^{\circ}$

Substituting the given values:
$210 = X_{\text{A}}(150) + (1 - X_{\text{A}})(300)$
$210 = 150X_{\text{A}} + 300 - 300X_{\text{A}}$
$210 = 300 - 150X_{\text{A}}$
$150X_{\text{A}} = 90$
$X_{\text{A}} = \dfrac{90}{150} = 0.6$

A common mistake is solving for the mole fraction of B ($0.4$) instead of A.

Answer: $0.6$

Assertion (A) is correct: Phenol reacts with bromine in non-polar solvents like $\text{CS}_{2}$ at low temperature ($273\text{ K}$) to give a mixture of ortho and para bromophenols. This is a monosubstitution reaction.

Reason (R) is correct: In aqueous medium, phenol ionizes to form the phenoxide ion. The phenoxide ion is much more activating than the $-\text{OH}$ group towards electrophilic aromatic substitution, leading to the formation of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

However, Reason (R) explains the polysubstitution reaction in aqueous medium, not the monosubstitution in $\text{CS}_{2}$. The correct explanation for Assertion (A) is that in non-polar solvents, the ionization of phenol is suppressed, and the $-\text{OH}$ group is less activating.

Thus, both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

119099.text:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion: Ketones react with ethylene glycol to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals in presence of dry HCl.
Reason: Dry hydrogen chloride protonates the oxygen of the carbonyl compounds and therefore, increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon facilitating the nucleophilic attack of glycol.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
119099.sol:
Assertion (A):
"Ketones react with ethylene glycol to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals in the presence of dry HCl ."
- This statement is correct. Ketones do react with ethylene glycol under acidic conditions (such as dry HCl) to form cyclic ketals. The dry HCl acts as a catalyst in this reaction, facilitating the formation of the ketal.
Reason (R):
"Dry hydrogen chloride protonates the oxygen of the carbonyl compounds and therefore increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon, facilitating the nucleophilic attack of glycol."
- This statement is also correct. The reasoning provided here accurately explains how dry HCl increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon by protonating the carbonyl oxygen. This makes the carbonyl carbon more susceptible to nucleophilic attack by ethylene glycol, leading to ketal formation.
Conclusion:
- Both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are correct.
- The Reason (R) correctly explains why the ketone reacts with ethylene glycol to form the cyclic ketal.
Thus, the correct answer is Option (1): "Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)."

120533.sol:
When a salt containing the chloride anion ($\text{Cl}^{-}$) is heated with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$) gas is evolved.

$\text{Cl}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \text{HSO}_4^{-}$

$\text{HCl}$ is a colourless gas with a pungent smell. When a glass rod dipped in aqueous ammonia ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) is brought near it, dense white fumes of ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) are formed.

$\text{HCl} + \text{NH}_3 \rightarrow \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ (dense white fumes)

Bromide gives reddish-brown fumes of $\text{Br}_2$, nitrate gives brown fumes of $\text{NO}_2$, and sulphate does not react with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to evolve such gases.

Answer: Chloride, $\text{Cl}^{-}$

121014.subject: Chemistry
121014.text: Which of the following deficiency diseases is caused by the specific water-soluble vitamin that is an exception because it can be stored in the human body?
121014.sol:
Water-soluble vitamins (B group and Vitamin C) are generally excreted in urine and cannot be stored in the body.

However, Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ is a notable exception as it is a water-soluble vitamin that can be stored in the liver.

According to NCERT, the deficiency of Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ causes pernicious anaemia, a condition where red blood cells are deficient in haemoglobin.

Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C (water-soluble, not stored), Beri-beri by Vitamin $\text{B}_{1}$ (water-soluble, not stored), and Night blindness by Vitamin A (fat-soluble).

Answer: Pernicious anaemia

121109.sol: There are also several organisms that you cannot see with your naked eye but they are all around you. If you were to increase the area that you make observations in, the range and variety of organisms that you see would increase. Obviously, if you were to visit a dense forest, you would probably see a much greater number and kinds of living organisms in it. Each different kind of plant, animal or organism that you see, represents a species. The number of species that are known and described range between 1.7-1.8 million. This refers to biodiversity or the number and types of organisms present on earth. We should remember here that as we explore new areas, and even old ones, new organisms are continuously being identified. As stated earlier, there are millions of plants and animals in the world; we know the plants and animals in our own area by their local names.

121357.subject: Botany
121357.text: What is the method of asexual reproduction in basidiomycetes?
121357.sol: Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi or puffballs. They grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps and in living plant bodies as parasites, e.g., rusts and smuts. The mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores are generally not found, but <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common. </mark> The sex organs are absent,but plasmogamy is brought about by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes. The resultant structure is dikaryotic which ultimately gives rise to basidium. Karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium producing four basidiospores. The basidiospores are exogenously produced on the basidium (pl.: basidia). The basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps. Some common members are Agaricus (mushroom), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus).

122746.subject: Botany
options: When the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction
When sepals or petals overlap one another in a particular direction
When sepals or petals just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping
When one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on
122746.sol: The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl is known as aestivation. The main types of aestivation are valvate, twisted, imbricate and vexillary (Figure 5.11). When sepals or petals in a whorl just touch one another at the margin, without overlapping, as in Calotropis, it is said to be valvate. If one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on as in china rose, lady’s finger and cotton, it is called twisted. If the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction as in Cassia and gulmohur, the aestivation is called imbricate. In pea and bean flowers, there are five petals, the largest (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings) which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel); this type of aestivation is known as vexillary or papilionaceous.

123003.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a cymose inflorescence, the youngest flowers or buds are present at the apex of the main axis.

Reason (R): The main axis in a cymose inflorescence terminates in a flower, limiting its further growth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
123003.sol:
The Assertion (A) is not correct. In a cymose inflorescence, the flowers are borne in a basipetal order. This means that the oldest flower is present at the apex and the younger flowers or buds are present towards the base.

The Reason (R) is correct. The main axis in a cymose inflorescence terminates in a flower, which limits its further growth. This early termination of the main axis is the reason why subsequent younger flowers arise laterally below it, resulting in the basipetal succession.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

125965.subject: Botany
125965.text: What components typically make up a seed?
options: Seed coat(s), embryo axis, fruit wall
125965.sol: In angiosperms, the seed is the final product of sexual reproduction. It is often described as a fertilised ovule. Seeds are formed inside fruits. A seed typically consists of seed coat(s), cotyledon(s) and an embryo axis. The cotyledons (Figure 1.15a) of the embryo are simple structures, generally thick and swollen due to storage of food reserves (as in legumes). Mature seeds may be non-albuminous or ex-albuminous. Nonalbuminous seeds have no residual endosperm as it is completely consumed during embryo development (e.g., pea, groundnut). Albuminous seeds retain a part of endosperm as it is not completely used up during embryo development (e.g., wheat, maize, barley, castor). Occasionally, in some seeds such as black pepper and beet, remnants of nucellus are also persistent

A fat is formed of two kinds of smaller molecules, i.e., glycerol and fatty acids. In making a fat three fatty acid molecules each jain to glycerol by an ester linkage. A fatty acid has a long carbon skeleton, usually 16 or 18 carbon atoms in length. It there are no double bonds between carbon atoms composing the chain, then as many hydrogen atoms as possible are bonded to the carbon skeleton.
This is called saturated fatty acid. Unsaturated fatty acid has one or more double bonds. Phosphoglycerides are esters of two fatty acids, phosphoric acid and a trifunctional alcohal glycerol. The fatty acids are attached to the glycerol at the 1 and 2 position an glycerol through ester bonds.

128346.subject: Zoology
128346.text: What is the main mineralocorticoid in our body?
128346.sol: The adrenal cortex can be divided into three layers, called zona reticularis (inner layer), zona fasciculata (middle layer) and zona glomerulosa (outer layer). The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones, commonly called as corticoids. The corticoids, which are involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called glucocorticoids. In our body, cortisol is the main glucocorticoid. Corticoids, which regulate the balance of water and electrolytes in our body are called mineralocorticoids. Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid in our body. Glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis; and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids. Cortisol is also involved in maintaining the cardio-vascular system as well as the kidney functions. Glucocorticoids, particularly cortisol, produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response. Cortisol stimulates the RBC production. Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water and excretion of K+ and phosphate ions. Thus, aldosterone helps in the maintenance of electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure.Small amounts of androgenic steroids are also secreted by the adrenal cortex which play a role in the growth of axial hair, pubic hair and facial hair during puberty.
